test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 08 Oct, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Who were the first foreign rulers of northwest India in the post-Mauryan period?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bactrian Greek**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bactrian Greeks were the first foreign rulers to establish control over northwest India following the decline of the Mauryan Empire.
 
• They were part of the Indo-Greek Kingdom, which was formed around 180 BCE after the Greco-Bactrian King Demetrius invaded India.
 
• The Indo-Greek Kingdom extended its influence over parts of modern-day Afghanistan, Pakistan, and northwestern India.
 
• The period of Indo-Greek rule is noted for the introduction of Hellenistic culture, art, and coinage in the region.
 
• The most renowned Indo-Greek ruler was Menander I (Milinda), who is celebrated for his dialogues with the Buddhist sage Nagasena, recorded in the Milinda Panha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indo-Greek Kingdom**

 
 
• The Indo-Greek Kingdom was established following the fragmentation of the Greco-Bactrian Kingdom, located in present-day Afghanistan and Central Asia.
 
• It is known for its fusion of Greek and Indian cultures, particularly in art and architecture.
 
• The kingdom played a significant role in the spread of Buddhism in Central Asia and India.
 
• Indo-Greek coinage is renowned for its artistic quality and bilingual inscriptions in Greek and Prakrit.
 
 
 
• **Menander I (Milinda)**
 
 
• Menander I was one of the most prominent Indo-Greek kings, who ruled from approximately 165 to 130 BCE.
 
• He is best known for his discussions on Buddhism with the sage Nagasena, which are recorded in the text "Milinda Panha" (The Questions of King Milinda).
 
• Menander's reign marked the zenith of the Indo-Greek influence in the Indian subcontinent.
 
 
 
• **Greco-Bactrian Kingdom**
 
 
• The Greco-Bactrian Kingdom was established around 256 BCE, following the fragmentation of Alexander the Great's empire.
 
• It was located in Bactria, present-day Afghanistan and parts of Central Asia.
 
• The kingdom is known for its rich cultural heritage and contributions to the spread of Hellenistic culture in Asia.
 
 
 
• **Decline of the Mauryan Empire**
 
 
• The Mauryan Empire began to decline after the death of Emperor Ashoka around 232 BCE.
 
• Internal conflicts and succession disputes weakened the central authority, leading to the fragmentation of the empire.
 
• The decline of the Mauryan Empire created a power vacuum that facilitated the emergence of foreign rulers like the Indo-Greeks in northwest India.
